svg.title: Shell jobs: background and foreground.
svg.desc: An interactive Bash with sleep available starts sleep 60 in the background. The prompt returns while sleep runs. jobs shows illustrative output [1]+ Running sleep 60 &, where 1 is the shell job number, not a process ID. For this single running job, fg %1 brings it to the foreground; Ctrl-C interrupts it and the prompt returns. Run the commands before the sixty seconds finish and use the number from your own jobs output. Background programs may still write to the terminal, and backgrounding does not make a service or promise survival after logout.
svg.text: SHELL JOBS: WHO HAS THE TERMINAL?
A job is a command or pipeline managed by your shell.
Foreground: the shell waits. Background: you get a prompt while the job runs.
Interactive Bash; sleep 60 waits 60 seconds. One job here; continue before it ends.
1 = job number, not a process ID. + marks the current job. Use your own job number.
%1 selects this shell's job 1, not PID 1. Use the job number from your own jobs output.
Background jobs can still print here. Background does not mean service or logout survival.
